title: Time's Up! (Edition 2)
author: David Ritchie
tagline: Can the government – or the public – spark the vital need for change?
description:
Our world has gone off the rails with abject failures by both governments and regulators.

Why? Why so much damage - in the UK and elsewhere manifested in: hugely expensive scandal after scandal; greed and corruption everywhere; government and leadership standards close to an all-time low; public services in dramatic decline; the justice system in disarray; the gap between rich and poor ever widening; overseas aid budgets cut; truth dismissed as fake news ... so much has gone wrong, without mentioning the catastrophic effects of Brexit and the pandemic.

Can genuine change occur?

It's long past time!

title: Neighbourhood Matters
author: Helgar Moore
tagline: Ordinary lives, extraordinary happenings, and life-changing secrets on a post-war regeneration scheme.

authors.name: Helgar Moore
authors.bio: Author and project manager at GB Publishing Org, exploring the human fabric, secrets, and interconnected lives of post-war British regeneration.

authorBio: Author and project manager at GB Publishing Org, exploring the human fabric, secrets, and interconnected lives of post-war British regeneration.
description:
A story about ordinary people, set on a newly built but ambitious post-war regeneration scheme from the late 1940’s. Having mixed ambitions and prospects, also different backgrounds, education and upbringing, it’s perhaps inevitable that, drawn together by location alone, they would interconnect in extraordinary ways.

Intrigue, in the same buildings, on the same street, as the characters arrive on the scene. Behind each painted door and house number, allocated by chance, ordinary lives are led to extraordinary happenings. A web of lies impacts others. Conspirers and prey, their lives interwoven.

Set at a time of social change, with expectations driving actions, decisions prove both life-changing and dangerous. Alternative morals create flashpoints, causing jealousy and betrayal, while driving relationships apart as well as in acts of kindness and support. Life is primarily focused on those who are closest.

Is the outcome, the unforeseen twist in the tale, justified?
